finding.claim: GET /mirror fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL server-side. The host guard at line 13 uses endswith with example.com and no leading dot or equality check, so hostnames like evilexample.com pass. An unauthenticated attacker can make the server send GET requests to attacker-controlled DNS names that resolve to internal, loopback, or link-local addresses, and learn the response body length.
finding.source: mirror.py:11 - query parameter url on unauthenticated GET /mirror
finding.sink: mirror.py:16 - httpx.AsyncClient().get(url) with the unmodified user string

trace.note: url: str is taken directly from the query string; the route has no auth dependency
host = urlparse(url).hostname or empty string; attacker controls the hostname
Only control: host.endswith('example.com'). No dot boundary, no equality, no port, scheme, or IP-range restriction. evilexample.com passes.
The same url is fetched; httpx resolves DNS at request time, so the attacker can point evilexample.com at an internal IP. DNS rebinding also works.
Response length is returned to the caller, giving a length-only response oracle.

finding.guards_checked: Hostname suffix check at lines 12-13: bypassed by any name ending in the characters example.com without a dot boundary. Userinfo and fragment tricks such as http://example.com@127.0.0.1 are rejected because urlparse().hostname returns the real host. Redirects: httpx AsyncClient defaults to follow_redirects=False in 0.20 and later, so 3xx responses are returned rather than followed; not verified against the installed version because the repo has no manifest. Scheme: not restricted in code; httpx rejects non-http schemes (unverified). Auth: none on /mirror. Port: unrestricted. Open, not reported: possible urlparse vs httpx authority parsing differential (for example backslash handling); needs the httpx source to check.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is mirror.py:13 `host.endswith("example.com")`, a suffix match with no dot boundary or equality, so it does not close the finding. ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 (".example.com") is defined but never used, so it is not a guard.
verdict.reason: The url query parameter (mirror.py:11) reaches the unauthenticated httpx.AsyncClient().get(url) at mirror.py:16, and the only host check at mirror.py:13 is a bare endswith("example.com") that accepts attacker-registered names like evilexample.com, so the server can be made to request internal addresses and return the body length (mirror.py:17).
